f) The poetic compositions of his brothers Sant Nivruttinath and Sant Sopandev and sister Muktabai are also well-known.

markup: Preamble of Indian Constitution
answermarkup:
i) The Preface to the Indian Constitution is called the Preamble.
ii) It sets out the objectives of our Constitution and tells us what we all have to achieve as a people.
iii) It consists of noble values, thoughts and ideas.
iv) It resolves to constitute India into a 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic'.
v) The Preamble begins with the words, 'We, the people of India'.
vi) It guarantees the Indian citizens the three values of Justice, Liberty and Equality.
vii) It ends with a mention of the fact that the people of India have given the Constitution to themselves.

markup: Travelogues
answermarkup:
i) The personal accounts of travels, written by the western travelers who came to India during the medieval period are called as travelogues.
ii) They are a type of written source of history.
iii) Some of the travelers who wrote travelogues are Al Biruni, Ibn Batuta, Niccolao Manucci.

markup: Socialist State
answermarkup:
i) A Socialist State is the one in which the gap between the rich and the poor is minimum.
ii) It emphasises on the value that all the people of the country have equal right over the wealth of the country.
iii) As a result, a socialist state ensures that wealth is not concentrated in the hands of a few people.

markup: Chakradhar Swami
answermarkup:
i) Chakradhar Swami founded the 'Mahanubhav Panth' in Maharashtra in the thirteenth century.
ii) Shri Govind Prabhu was the Guru of Chakradhar Swami.
iii) Chakradhar Swami preached devotion to Krishna and supported equality.
iv) Men and women belonging to all castes and creeds followed him.
v) He travelled to all parts of Maharashtra to preach.
vi) He preached in Marathi instead of Sanskrit and many of his works were composed in Marathi. This led to the development of the Marathi language.

markup: Constitutional Remedies
answermarkup:
Courts have powers to issue various kinds of writs in order to protect the rights of the citizens. These writs are as follows:
i. Habeas Corpus: It ensures our protection from unlawful arrest and detention.
ii. Mandamus: It is the order of the Supreme Court or the High Court commanding the government to perform an action that is its duty to perform in public interest.
iii. Prohibition: It prevents a subordinate court from exceeding its jurisdiction.
iv. Quo Warranto: It is used to restrain a person from acting in an office to which he is not entitled.
v. Certiorari: The order to remove a law suit from a subordinate court to a superior court.

markup: The Coronation of Shivaji Maharaj
answermarkup:
i) The foundation of Maratha Swaraj involved a continuous struggle for over thirty years.
ii) Shivaji Maharaj realised that a formal coronation was necessary for the Swaraj to win general recognition as a sovereign independent State.
iii) There were two traditions of religious ceremonies in India - Vedic and Tantric. Shivaji Maharaj honoured both the traditions and had two coronation ceremonies performed.
iv) On 6th June 1674, Shivaji Maharaj had himself coronated at Raigad by Pandit Gagabhatt. On 24th September 1674, he had his second coronation performed under the guidance of Nischalpuri Gosavi.
Through these coronations, Shivaji Maharaj became 'Chhatrapati' of the Swaraj.

markup: Sovereign State
answermarkup:
i) Sovereign State is a state which is not under the control of a foreign power.
ii) Attaining sovereignty was the most important goal of our freedom struggle, which meant to have the ultimate authority to govern ourselves.
iii) In a democracy, sovereignty rests with the people of the State, who elect their representatives and the government elected by the people makes laws on behalf of the people.
iv) Thus, our Constitution reflects the principle of sovereignty.

markup: Conflict with the Afghans
answermarkup:
i. The Marathas chastised the Rohillas who had migrated from Afghanistan to Rohilkhand.
ii. The ruler of Afghanistan, Ahmadshah Abdali, who was attracted by the riches of India and wanted to bring the region up to Punjab under Afghanistan, attacked Punjab in 1751 CE.
iii. As there was anarchy in the Mughal territory, the Mughal Emperor sought help from Marathas to protect Delhi from the threat of Abdali's invasion. He signed a treaty with the Marathas in April 1752 to protect the Mughal power from enemies like the Rohillas, the Jats, the Rajputs and the Afghans.
iv. In return, the Marathas were given the right to collect Chauthai in the territories of Punjab, Multan, Rajputana, Sindh and Rohilkhand and the Subhedari of Ajmer and Agra provinces.
v. As per the treaty, the Peshwa sent the Shinde-Holkar armies to protect Delhi on behalf of the Chhatrapati. On hearing that the Marathas were marching to Delhi, Abdali went back to his country.
vi. Since Abdali's threat got averted, the Emperor gave the Marathas, Chauthai rights to the Mughal subhas of Kabul, Kandahar and Peshawar which were a part of Abdali's Afghanistan.
vii. According to the treaty, it was the Marathas' duty to win back these subhas from Abdali.
viii. A conflict ensued between Abdali and the Marathas which further led to the Third Battle of Panipat.
ix. Abdali invaded India six times during this period.

markup: Standard of living in Maratheshahi
answermarkup:
i. In Maratheshahi, majority of people resided in villages that were mostly self-sufficient. Only salt had to be imported from other places.
ii. The needs of farmers were limited as they grew jowar, bajra, wheat, ragi, maize, rice and other grains in their fields. Their daily diet consisted of bhakari, onion, chutney and an accompaniment.
iii. Rich people's diet consisted of rice, dal, chapatis, vegetables, salads, milk and dahi products.
iv. The houses in the village were made of mud and bricks. Wadas with one or two storeys were seen in cities.
v. In Maratheshahi, men wore a dhoti, kurta, angarakha and mundase; whereas women wore nineyard sarees and blouses.
vi. They used a barter system for everyday transactions.

markup: Fundamental Duties of Citizens
answermarkup:
i) These duties remind citizens of their responsibilities towards the nation.
ii) They include respecting the Constitution, National Flag, and National Anthem.
iii) Citizens must protect the environment, promote harmony, and safeguard public property.
iv) Every parent must provide education to children between 6 and 14 years of age.

markup: Sant Tukaram
answermarkup:
a) He was a great Sant who belonged to Dehu near Pune. He stressed that devotion should have morality along with it.
b) His abhangas are very pleasing, simple & clear and poetically rich.
c) Sant Tukaram's work 'Gatha' is a precious treasure of the Marathi language.
d) He asked people to find god by loving the unhappy and tormented. To show this idea by practising it, he threw away the documents of the loans that people had borrowed from him in the river Indrayani and freed many families from the burden of loans.
e) He criticised the hypocrisy and superstition in the society in very strong terms. Some people opposed his ideas of social awakening and threw his abhangas in the Indrayani river.
f) His disciples and associates were of different castes and creeds. Gangarampant Maval and Santaji Jagnade wrote down his abhangas.

markup: The First Battle of Panipat
answermarkup:
i) Ibrahim Lodi was the Sultan of Delhi and Daulatkhan Lodi was a Governor of Punjab.
ii) The relationship between Ibrahim Lodi and Daulatkhan Lodi became strained and he invited Babur to march against Ibrahim Lodi.
iii) Taking advantage of this opportunity, Babur invaded India.
iv) A battle was fought between Ibrahim Lodi and Babur on 21st April 1526 at Panipat.
v) In this battle, Babur made use of effective artillery for the first time in India and defeated Ibrahim Lodi's army.
This battle is known as the First Battle of Panipat.

markup: Rani Durgavati
answermarkup:
i) Rani Durgavati was born in the Chandel Rajput dynasty.
ii) After she married, she became the queen of Gondvana which comprised of the eastern part of Vidarbha, part of Madhya Pradesh, western part of today's Chhattisgarh, northern part of Andhra Pradesh and the western part of Odisha.
iii) She was an excellent administrator.
iv) Mughals wanted to capture Gondvana. In order to save Gondvana, she put up a brave struggle against the Mughals.
v) After her husband's death, Durgavati laid down her life while fighting against Akbar, but she did not surrender.
vi) Her struggle against the Mughals is important in medieval history.

markup: Meerabai
answermarkup:
i) Sant Meerabai was one of the proponents of the Bhakti Movement.
ii) She belonged to the royal family of Mewad but renounced all pleasures of the royal family and devoted herself completely to Lord Krishna.
iii) She composed verses in Rajasthani and Gujarati, giving the message of devotion, tolerance and humanity through them.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj's Ashtapradhan Mandal
answermarkup:
i) Shivaji Maharaj had set up an efficient administration for the smooth management of the Swaraj and to ensure people's welfare.
ii) He divided the administration into eight departments and appointed a head for each department. Pradhan, Amatya, Sachiv, Mantri, Senapati, Sumant, Nyayadhish and Panditrao were these eight heads.
iii) These eight ministers, who were selected on the basis of their merit and achievements constituted the Ashtapradhan Mandal.
iv) Maharaj alone had the power to appoint or remove a minister of the council. The ministers were answerable to the Maharaj for the administration of their departments.
v) They were paid handsome salaries instead of jagirs, vatans, gifts or fiefs.

markup: Right to Freedom of Religion
answermarkup:
i) Every citizen of India has the freedom to follow and practise any religion.
ii) Citizens can establish institutions for religious purposes.
iii) The State cannot collect or impose religious taxes.
iv) Religious education cannot be made compulsory in government-aided schools.

markup: Guru Gobindsingh
answermarkup:
i) Guru Gobindsingh became the Guru of the Sikhs after Aurangzeb imprisoned and beheaded Guru Tegbahaddar in 1675 CE.
ii) He continued the struggle of Guru Tegbahaddar.
iii) He organised his followers into a fighting force called the 'Khalsa Dal' and encouraged their martial spirit.
iv) They were headquartered at Anandpur. Aurangzeb attacked Anandpur to fight the Sikhs.
v) The Sikhs fought back fiercely but they could not succeed.
vi) Later in 1708 CE, Guru Gobindsingh came to the Deccan.
vii) There was an attempt on his life when he was at Nanded and soon after, he succumbed to his wounds.

markup: Bajirao I
answermarkup:
i. Bajirao I was a courageous and great general who established the Maratha supremacy in the North and also won status for the Martha power as a formidable power in the entire India.
ii. He was the son of Balaji Vishwanath and was appointed as the Peshwa by Shahu Maharaj in 1720 CE after the death of Balaji.
iii. Bajirao expanded the Maratha Empire during his 20 year term.
iv. When the Mughal Subhedar of Deccan, Nizam - ul - Mulk, went against the Maratha's rights to recover Chauthai - Sardeshmukhi from the Mughal areas and captured some part of the Pune Pargana, Bajirao decided to counter him. He defeated the Nizam, at Palkhed near Aurangabad and got back the rights of collecting the revenue.
v. He strengthened the Maratha power in Malwa and Bundelkhand, by helping King Chhatrasal against Bangush.
vi. While on his march on Delhi in 1737 CE, he defeated the Nizam at Bhopal and secured the sanad of Malwa subhedari for the Marathas.
vii. He sent Malharrao Holkar, Ranoji Shinde and Udaji Pawar under the leadership of his brother Chimajiappa to conquer the Vasai and Thane territories from the Portuguese.
viii. Bajirao I died at Raverkhedi on the banks of the Narmada in April 1740, while he was on his way to defend the Mughals from the invasion by Nadirshah, the Emperor of Iran.

markup: Process of Amending the Constitution
answermarkup:
i) The makers of the Constitution realized that there may be a need to make changes or amendments in the Constitution as per the demands of the changing times.
ii) Hence, they made provisions for such amendments in the Constitution itself. Accordingly, amendments are done through a specific procedure.
iii) This procedure is unique and is flexible enough to easily bring about general amendments.
iv) Also, as frequent amendments to Constitution can lead to a situation of instability, it is necessary to ensure that an amendment is made only after giving it a careful consideration.
v) Hence, the Constitution leaves a lot of scope for consideration and thought before bringing about important amendments.

markup: Chimajiappa
answermarkup:
i. Chimajiappa was the brother of Peshwa Bajirao I.
ii. Under his leadership, the Marathas strengthened their posts in Malwa.
iii. He conquered the Thane and adjacent areas from the Portuguese.
iv. In 1739 CE, he laid siege to the Vasai fort and continued it with perseverance against the strong Portuguese. He forced them to surrender and got the Vasai fort and the other Portuguese territory under the Marathas.

markup: The Battle of Palkhed
answermarkup:
i. Nizam - ul - Mulk was appointed as the Subhedar of Deccan by the Mughal Emperor Farukhsear.
ii. Nizam tried to establish his separate existence at Hyderabad in 1713 CE.
iii. He was against the Mughal Emperor's decision of giving the Marathas the right to recover Chauthai - Sardeshmukhi from the Mughal areas.
iv. He captured some part of the Pune Pargana, but got defeated by Bajirao I in the battle of Palkhed near Aurangabad.
v. Thereafter, the Nizam accepted the Maratha right to collect Chauthai - Sardeshmukhi.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj's campaign of the South
answermarkup:
i) Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj undertook a campaign of the South in October 1677, after three years of coronation.
ii) He went to Golconda, where he called on the Qutubshah and entered into a treaty of friendship with him.
iii) Later, Shivaji Maharaj won Bengaluru, Hoskote in Karnataka, Jinji, Vellore, etc. forts in Tamil Nadu and some other territories of Adilshah.
iv) He appointed Raghunath Narayan Hanamante as the chief administrator to look after these conquered territories.

markup: Consequences of battle of Ashti
answermarkup:
i. After the defeat of the Marathas in the battle of Ashti in Solapur district in 1818 CE, the Maratha power came to an end.
ii. The British gained control over a major part of India.
iii. Because of this, India was exposed to the Western world, which led to many changes in India's social system. Many old customs and superstitions came to an end and India went into a major transformation.
iv. Thus, the medieval period of Indian history came to an end and the Modern period began.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj’s Struggle and Foundation of Swaraj
answermarkup: Before the foundation of Swaraj, Maharashtra was under the control of the Adilshahi, Siddi, Portuguese, and Mughal powers. Shivaji Maharaj fought bravely against all of them and established an independent and sovereign Swaraj, which he later transformed into Surajya—a kingdom devoted to the welfare of all.

markup: Oral sources
answermarkup:
i) The various forms of literature like owis, folk songs, folk tales, legends etc. which are traditionally passed on from one generation to the other by the word of mouth are called as oral sources of history.
ii) Oral sources reveal various aspects of people's lives.
iii) They help us understand various historical events, the policies and administrations of various rulers and the diplomatic relations between them.
iv) They also throw light on the religious co-ordination, financial transactions, economic conditions and technological advancements of that period.
v) Some of the examples of oral sources are: Myths, Folk songs, Gatha, Shlokas, Abhangas, Powadas, Proverbs and Legends.

markup: The valour shown by Mahadji Shinde
answermarkup:
i. Mahadji Shinde was as brave and astute as his father Ranoji Shinde. Therefore, he was given the family title of Sardar by Peshwa Madhavrao.
ii. He restored the Maratha supremacy and reputation in the North, which was lost after the Maratha defeat at Panipat.
iii. Realising that the guerilla tactics were not enough for the plains of the North, he trained his army and modernised his artillery under the guidance of de Boigne, a French military expert. With the help of this trained army, he subdued the Rohillas, the Jats, the Rajputs and the Bundellas.
iv. Mahadji Shinde defeated the British when they tried to capture the Emperor of Delhi and also when they marched on the Marathas via Borghat.
v. He also defeated Najib Khan's grandson Ghulam Kadir when he captured the Red Fort and tortured the Emperor and his begums for their wealth. Mahadji also reinstated the Emperor on the throne of Delhi.
vi. Mahadji defeated the difficult situations with strong determination and looked after the Delhi affairs during 1784 CE to 1794 CE.

markup: The Maratha rule in Gujarat
answermarkup:
i. The foundation of Maratha power in Gujarat was laid by Khanderao Dabhade and his son Trimbakrao.
ii. After the death of Khanderao, his wife Umabai defeated the Mughal Sardar of Ahmadabad and conquered the fort there.
iii. Later, the Gaikwads made Vadodara in Gujarat a seat of their pow

markup: Peshwa Madhavrao
answermarkup:
i. Peshwa Madhavrao succeeded his father Peshwa Nanasaheb after his death.
ii. During his reign, Peshwa Madhavrao kept the Nizam and Hyder Ali at bay. He defeated the Nizam at Rakshasbhuvan near Paithan.
iii. He re-established the Maratha supremacy in the north after the Battle of Panipat.
iv. He is described as an honest, hard-working and determined administrator who was keen on public welfare.
v. He dug many wells in Pune and increased the water supply to the city and also ensured the welfare of the farmers.
vi. Under his rule, administrators like Nana Phadnavis and judges like Ramshashtri Prabhune emerged. He reformed the judiciary for better justice to common people, started the artillery and ammunition factories and even established a mint to make coins.

markup: Intelligence Department of Swaraj
answermarkup:
i) The intelligence department of Shivaji Maharaj was responsible for getting precise and timely information about the movements of the enemy and submitting it to Maharaj.
ii) The department was very efficient and it helped him protect the Swaraj from the enemies.
iii) Bahirji Naik was the head of the intelligence department and was extremely skilled at his job.
iv) He had successfully collected precise and detailed information about Surat before raiding it.

markup: Equality of opportunity
answermarkup:
i) Equality is one of the three values as guaranteed by the Preamble of Indian Constitution to its citizens.
ii) This is in terms of equality of status and equality of opportunity.
iii) Equality of opportunity emphasises on the opportunity for development to every citizen without any discrimination on the basis of caste, creed, race etc.

markup: Azamshah released Shahu Maharaj from captivity.
answermarkup:
1.	After Aurangzeb’s death, his sons fought for the Mughal throne.
2.	Azamshah wanted to weaken the Maratha power.
3.	He believed that releasing Shahu Maharaj would cause conflict between Shahu and Maharani Tarabai.
4.	This internal struggle, he thought, would reduce Maratha strength.

markup: Aurangzeb turned his attention towards Adilshahi and Qutubshahi kingdoms.
answermarkup:
i. The high resistance offered by the Marathas made Aurangzeb realise that fighting with Marathas was difficult.
ii. The Marathas, with their bravery and valour, had foiled all his attempts at conquering the Maratha territories.
iii. As a result, Aurangzeb did not succeed in his campaign against the Marathas which made him feel helpless and frustrated.
iv. Therefore, he finally suspended the campaign and turned towards the Adilshahi and Qutubshahi kingdoms to conquer them.

markup: Titles like Raja, Maharaja, and Raobahadur were abolished by the Constitution.
answermarkup: Because such titles created artificial divisions and a sense of superiority among people. To maintain equality and discourage social hierarchy, the Constitution abolished all titles.

markup: The Rajputs fought against the Mughals.
answermarkup:
i) With his policy of amicable relations, Akbar had secured the cooperation of the Rajputs.
ii) However, Aurangzeb could not get the same.
iii) Aurangzeb annexed the kingdom of Marwad to the Mughal Empire after the death of Rana Jaswantsingh.
iv) However, Durgadas Rathod fought hard against the Mughals and crowned Jaswantsingh's minor son Ajitsingh as the King of Marwad.
Thus, we can see that in order to maintain their independence, the Rajputs fought against the Mughals.

markup: Shivaji protected the salt industry in Konkan.
answermarkup:
i) Shivaji Maharaj knew that a kingdom cannot prosper without an increase in trade and hence it was his policy to protect industries.
ii) At that time, the local trade of the salt industry was affected as the traders imported salt into Swaraj from Portuguese territory.
iii) Shivaji Maharaj charged heavy duty on this salt import so as to increase its cost and lead to decline in its import.
iv) This resulted in an increase of the sale of the local salt.
In this way, Shivaji Maharaj protected the salt industry in Konkan.

markup: Women’s life during the Maratha period was full of hardships.
answermarkup:
i) Women were confined to household duties only.
ii) Customs like child marriage, polygamy, and sati restricted their freedom.
iii) Their education was neglected, and only a few women like Jijabai and Tarabai gained prominence.

markup: The Bahamani Kingdom disintegrated into five fragments.
answermarkup:
i) After the Chief Wazir of the Bahamani Kingdom - Mahmud Gawan - died, there was an increase in factionism among the Bahamani Sardars.
ii) Also, conflict with the Vijaynagar Kingdom had an adverse effect on the Bahamani kingdom.
iii) The provincial Governors began to act more independently.
iv) As a result, the Bahamani kingdom disintegrated into five small fragments Imadshahi of Varhad, Baridshahi of Bidar, Adilshahi of Bijapur, Nizamshahi of Ahmadnagar and Qutubshahi of Golconda.

markup: The Marathas became powerful in North and South India.
answermarkup:
•	The brave Sardar families like Holkars, Shindes, Bhosales, and Gaikwads expanded Maratha power.
•	They fought bravely and established control over large territories.
•	They worked unitedly under the leadership of the Peshwas.

markup: Different communities have the right to preserve their language and culture.
answermarkup: Because the Constitution grants Cultural and Educational Rights so that every community can protect and promote its unique identity, traditions, and literature.

markup: Mahadji Shinde is called the restorer of Maratha prestige in North India.
answermarkup:
•	After the defeat at Panipat, he revived Maratha power in the North.
•	He modernised his army with the help of the French officer de Boigne.
•	He defeated the Rohillas, Jats, and Rajputs.
•	He reinstated the Emperor on the throne of Delhi and gained the title Vakil-i-Mutlak.

markup: Delhi needed the help from the Marathas.
answermarkup:
i. The Mughal power faced the threat of invasion from Iran and Afghan and also of the local Pathan, local Rajput, Jat and Rohilas rulers.
ii. Aurangzeb's successors were fighting amongst themselves. The Delhi court was marked by bickering and confusion.
iii. The internal competition and struggle in the court had also weakened the Mughal power.
Hence, Delhi needed the help from the Marathas.

markup: The Emperor entered into a treaty with the Marathas in April 1752.
answermarkup:
i. The Mughals faced the threat of an invasion by Ahmadshah Abdali, when he attacked Punjab in 1751 CE.
ii. During this time, there was anarchy in the Mughal territory.
iii. The Emperor was sure that only the Maratha strength and integrity could provide protection to Delhi.
iv. So they sought the help of the Marathas and entered into a treaty with them ensuring protection to the Mughals against the enemies like the Rohillas, the Jats, the Rajputs and the Afghans.

markup: The battle of Wadgaon was important in Maratha history.
answermarkup:
•	The British army was defeated by the Marathas.
•	The British were forced to surrender Raghunathrao to the Marathas.
•	It proved the strength and unity of the Marathas under Mahadji Shinde.

markup: The British were forced to surrender the custody of Raghunathrao to the Marathas.
answermarkup:
i. Due to the family disputes amongst the Peshwas, Raghunathrao went to the British camp as he wanted to become a Peshwa with the help of the British.
ii. The Maratha Statesmen were against this and this led to an inevitable conflict between the Marathas and the British.
iii. The British marched on the Marathas via Borghat from Mumbai.
iv. The Maratha army under the leadership of Mahadaji Shinde blocked the supply of foodgrains to the British, using guerrilla tactics.
v. Both the armies met at Wadgaon and the British were defeated in this battle.
It-was then that the British were forced to surrender the custody of Raghunathrao to the Marathas.

markup: Rana Sanga's army was defeated.
answermarkup:
i) Rana Sanga was the king of Mewad.
ii) After Babur won the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 CE, Rana Sanga united all Rajput kings against Babur.
iii) There was a battle between Babur and Rana Sanga at Khanua.
iv) However, in this battle, Babur had an edge over Rana Sanga with resources like his artillery and a reserved force at his disposal. These played a key role in Babur's victory.
Thus, Rana Sanga's army was defeated.

markup: Sant Kabir became a renowned Sant in the Bhakti movement.
answermarkup:
i) Sant Kabir did not attach any importance to places of pilgrimage, vratas or idol worship and did not believe in any differences based on caste, creed, sect and religion. Rather, he believed that truth itself was God.
ii) He strongly criticized the people who were extremely orthodox in both Hindu and Muslim religions and preached equality of all human beings and wanted to bring about Hindu and Muslim unity.
iii) His compositions are also included in the Guru Granth Sahib.
iv) Bhakti movement too did not give unnecessary importance to hierarchies and emphasized harmony between the different sects and religions and devotion to God.
Since, Sant Kabir's preaching was aligned to the main principle of the Bhakti movement; he became a renowned Sant in the Bhakti movement.

markup: Two separate Maratha States were formed.
answermarkup:
i. Shahu Maharaj marched towards Maharashtra after his release from the Mughal prince Azamshah.
ii. He was joined by a few Maratha Sardars but Maharani Tarabai declined his claim to the throne of the Maratha Chhatrapati.
iii. Shahu Maharaj's army fought with the army of Maharani Tarabai at Khed on the banks of the Bheema and won the battle. He captured Satara and made it the capital of his kingdom. He got himself crowned.
iv. Maharani Tarabai proclaimed her minor son Shivaji II as Chhatrapati at Pahnala in 1710 CE. Kolhapur was the capital of this independent kingdom.
v. This mutual opposition between Maharani Tarabai and Shahu Maharaj continued.
Thus, two separate Maratha States were formed, one at Kolhapur and the other at Satara.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj took an aggressive stand against the Mughals.
answermarkup:
i) Shivaji Maharaj did not want any conflict with the Mughals immediately after returning from Agra.
ii) However, he wanted to recapture the forts and territories given to the Mughals as per the Treaty of Purandar.
iii) For this, he prepared a comprehensive and a bold plan. It was his strategy to capture the forts by sending a well-equipped army and at the same time, keep the Mughals unstable by invading the territories of the Deccan under the control.
In this way, Shivaji Maharaj took an aggressive stand against the Mughals.

markup: A stone inscription is considered to be an authentic source of history.
answermarkup:
i) An inscription refers to the carving on a stone, a wall, etc. Few examples of such are - inscriptions found in the Brihadishwara temple in Tanjavur; inscriptions from the period of Chalukya, Rashtrakuta, Chola and Yadav kings.
ii) Inscriptions are a type of material source.
iii) Inscriptions provide authentic information about individuals, society, place and time which are considered as vital factors from the point of view of history.
iv) Through inscriptions, we also get information about the various features like language, script and the social life of the past period. Such data can be considered to be authentic.
Hence, a stone inscription is considered to be an authentic source of history.

markup: India is a Republic State.
answermarkup: i) A Republic is the one where none of the public positions are inherited through hereditary succession. ii) The People of a republic elect these representatives unlike monarchy where the positions are occupied by the members of a single family on the basis of heredity. iii) Some examples of public positions are as follows a. The President b. The Prime Minister c. The Governor d. The Chief Minister e. The Mayor f. The Sarpanch iv) Any Indian citizen fulfilling the required age criterion for a desired public position can get himself/herself elected to it. v) India has adopted this value and hence, India is a Republic State.

markup: Fundamental Duties were included in the Constitution.
answermarkup:
i. The government has made various schemes for the people's welfare.
ii. The benefits of these schemes cannot reach all people if they do not fulfil their Fundamental Duties.
iii. For this, it is required that the Indian citizens become conscious of their responsibilities.
iv. In order to bring about this consciousness, Fundamental Duties were included in the Constitution.

markup: Citizens can approach the court if their fundamental rights are violated.
answermarkup: Because the Constitution provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, which allows citizens to seek justice and protection of their rights through the Supreme Court or High Courts.

markup: Maratha architecture reached great heights during the Peshwa period.
answermarkup:
i) The Peshwas built beautiful wadas, temples, ghats, and water systems.
ii) Skilled architects and artists like Hiroji Indulkar worked during this period.
iii) Temples like Kalaram and forts like Shaniwarwada show their architectural excellence.

markup: Veermata Jijabai was a competent and visionary political expert.
answermarkup:
i) At a young age, Jijabai had received military training as well as education in various subjects.
ii) She helped and encouraged Shahaji Maharaj to realize his dream of establishing Swaraj. Also constantly guided Shivaji in the mission of establishing Swaraj.
iii) At times, she also undertook the task of giving verdicts for resolving the problems of people.
iv) She was very particular about giving excellent education to Shivaji and instilled values like modesty, truthfulness, oratory, vigilance, courage and fearlessness in him. She kept a check that he was trained in the usage of weapons and inspired in him, the will to win and the dream of Swaraj. Because of these different aspects of Jijabai, we can say that, she was a competent and visionary political expert.

markup: Azamshah released Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj from his custody
answermarkup:
i. There was a fight after Emperor Aurangzeb's death among his sons for the throne of Delhi.
ii. Prince Azamshah, his son, marched towards Delhi from the South to seize the imperial throne.
iii. Prince Shahu was in his captivity and he believed that there would be a conflict between Maharani Tarabai and Shahu Maharaj for the gadi of the Maratha Chhatrapati.
iv. Such a conflict would make the Maratha strength weak.
Hence, Azamshah released Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj from his custody.

markup: Sant Eknath was a teacher of the people in the true sense of the term.
answermarkup:
i) Sant Eknath composed many abhangas, gavalans, bharuds, etc.
ii) He stated Bhagvat Dharma in a simple manner.
iii) In Bhavarth Ramayan, he portrayed people's life through the story of Ram.
iv) He explained the Bhakti part of the Sanskrit Bhagvat in Marathi.
v) Through his own conduct, he demonstrated that there is no need to renounce worldly matters for attaining the highest truth, paramarth.
Hence, it is rightly said that, Sant Eknath, he was a teacher of the people in the true sense of the term.

markup: The State cannot impose religious taxes.
answermarkup: Because India is a secular country and every religion is treated equally. Imposing religious taxes would mean promoting one religion over another, which is against the right to freedom of religion.

markup: The villages were self-sufficient in Shivaji's times.
answermarkup:
i) Agriculture was the backbone of the economy during the reign of Shivaji Maharaj.
ii) Many occupations developed to supplement agriculture.
iii) Artisans in the villages produced goods and fulfilled the needs of the local people. They received 'Baluta', a share of agricultural produce from the farmers.
In this manner, villages were self-sufficient in Shivaji's times.

markup: Why Shahaji Maharaj is termed a Swaraj visionary?
answermarkup:
i) Shahaji Maharaj was a pre-eminent Sardar in Deccan region.
ii) He was a courageous, valiant and a great political expert. He had all the qualities of a great King and a supreme great leader.
iii) He had won many regions in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. He loved his subjects and aspired to establish Swaraj by ousting the powers of foreign people.
iv) He had arranged for providing excellent education to Shivaji so as to enable him to become a great king.
Due to all these reasons, Shahaji Maharaj is known as Swaraj visionary.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj started his work of founding Swaraj in the Maval region.
answermarkup:
i) Maval region in the Sahyadris was in the Pune jagir of Shivaji Maharaj.
ii) The Maval region consists of hills and valleys and hence is not easily accessible.
iii) Shivaji Maharaj made use of the above geographical features skillfully for fighting the mighty Adilshahi to lay the foundation of the Swaraj.
Hence, Shivaji Maharaj started the work of founding the Swaraj in the Maval region.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj entered into a treaty with the Adilshah.
answermarkup:
i) While Shivaji Maharaj was trapped at Panhala, Aurangzeb, who had ascended the throne of Delhi, sent Shaistakhan to the Deccan.
ii) Shaistakhan invaded the Pune province.
iii) Even at that time, the conflict between Shivaji Maharaj and Adilshah continued.
iv) Shivaji Maharaj then realized that it would not be prudent to fight two enemies at the same time.
Therefore, after escaping from Panhalgad and reaching Vishalgad safely, he entered into a treaty with Adilshah.

markup: The State shall protect all monuments of historic interest.
answermarkup:
i. All monuments of historic interest like artefacts, buildings, etc. give a lot of information about the rich cultural heritage of the country.
ii. Some of these monuments tell us about the inspiring story of India's freedom struggle, the reigns and rulers of the past etc.
Hence, the State shall protect all monuments of historic interest.

markup: Aurangzeb realised that fighting with Marathas was difficult.
answermarkup:
i. Aurangzeb had a misconception that the Maratha rule would come to an end once the Maratha forts were captured.
ii. So he put a siege around Ramsej fort near Nashik. Aurangzeb's army was huge.
iii. In spite of being small, the Maratha army fought with perseverance for five years with was unparalleled bravery.
This resistance offered by the Marathas made Aurangzeb realise that fighting with Marathas was difficult.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj’s army was disciplined and loyal.
answermarkup: Because Maharaj maintained strict discipline, paid soldiers’ salaries in cash and on time, and honoured brave warriors. He also cared for the families of those who died in battle, which earned him their loyalty.

markup: Aurangzeb imprisoned Guru Tegbahaddar.
answermarkup:
i) Guru Tegbahaddar was the ninth Guru of the Sikhs.
ii) During his time, Aurangzeb was the Mughal emperor.
iii) Aurangzeb had a policy of religious intolerance.
iv) This policy was strongly protested by Guru Tegbahaddar.
Hence, Aurangzeb imprisoned Guru Tegbahaddar and beheaded him in 1675 CE.

markup: Mahadji Shinde defeated Kadir.
answermarkup:
i. The heirs of Najib Khan who were responsible for the battle of Panipat, were still plotting against the Marathas in Rohilkhand.
ii. Najib Khan's grandson Ghulam Kadir captured the Red Fort.
iii. He tortured the Emperor and his begums for their wealth. He removed the Emperor's eyes and took hold of the royal treasure.
iv. In these circumstances, Mahadji defeated Kadir. He recovered the wealth from him and returned it to the Emperor. He reinstated the Emperor on the throne of Delhi and controlled the politics of India by putting the Emperor under Maratha control.

markup: Why has the Constitution created an independent Judiciary for India?
answermarkup:
i) The disputes which are not mutually resolved are referred to the Judiciary.
ii) The Court hears both the contesting parties and then looks into the entire matter.
iii) If it feels that there is any injustice, it passes its judgement accordingly, to level the fields. This has to be done impartially.
iv) To achieve this impartiality, the Constitution created an independent Judiciary for India.
v) The Constitution has made provisions like appointment of the judges by the President and not by the Government, to ensure that the independence of the judiciary is maintained.

markup: Ganeshotsava was celebrated with great importance during the Peshwa period.
answermarkup:
i) The Peshwas were great devotees of Lord Ganesha.
ii) They personally took part in Ganeshotsav celebrations every year.
iii) Hence, the festival gained social and cultural significance across Maharashtra.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj is known for his religious tolerance.
answermarkup: Because he respected people of all religions, employed Muslims in high positions, and gave orders to protect mosques and the Holy Quran during military campaigns.

markup: It was decided that the Raigad fort should be fought under the leadership of Maharani Yesubai.
answermarkup:
i. After the death of Sambhaji Maharaj, Aurangzeb thought that his dream of winning the Maratha kingdom would come true and hence, he sent Zulfikarkhan to put Raigad under siege.
ii. During this time, Rajaram Maharaj, his wife Maharani Tarabai, Sambhaji Maharaj's wife Maharani Yesubai and his son Shahu were in Raigad. But, all members of the royal family staying at one place was risky.
iii. Maharani Yesubai bravely resolved that she would not surrender to the Mughals under any conditions and took many important political decisions on Raigad.
iv. She decided that Rajaram Maharaj should escape from Raigad and go to a far off place like Jinji.
It was thus decided that in the absence of Rajaram Maharaj, the fight to defend Raigad would continue under the leadership of Maharani Yesubai.

markup: The British replaced the Marathas as the main power in India.
answermarkup:
•	After Mahadji Shinde and Nana Phadanvis died, the Marathas became weak.
•	Peshwa Bajirao II lacked leadership qualities.
•	Internal conflicts among the Sardars weakened their unity.
•	The British took advantage and defeated the Marathas in 1818 CE.

markup: Sambhaji Maharaj had to abandon the winning campaign of Goa and return to fight with the Mughals.
answermarkup:
i. The Portuguese of Goa had joined hands with Aurangzeb against Sambhaji Maharaj. In order to teach them a lesson, he attacked the Revdanda fort of the Portuguese in 1683 CE.
ii. To counter this, the Portuguese laid attack to the Fonda fort of the Marathas on the Goa border.But, the Marathas broke through the siege and attacked Goa. Yesaji Kank showed great valour in the battle.
iii. The Portuguese Governor got wounded and retreated but Sambhaji Maharaj followed him landing the Portuguese in deep trouble.
iv. Exactly at the same time, the Mughals attacked the South Konkan region of Marathas.
Hearing this, Sambhaji Maharaj had to abandon the winning campaign of Goa and return to fight with the Mughals.

markup: The teachings of the Sants developed the moral sensibilities of society in Maharashtra.
answermarkup:
i) The Sants gave the message of equality and humanity to people. They preached that people should live together in harmony, unity and love, leaving aside pride arising out of caste and varna.
ii) They protected the society from a deterioration of ethics and religion by showing them the true meaning of religion and simplified the complex dharma of the scholars in the language of the people.
iii) The Sants taught that everyone is equal before god.
iv) They carried on their duties even as they were engaged in devotion.
Thus, the Sants developed the moral sensibilities of the society in Maharashtra through their teachings and their own example.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj raised a navy.
answermarkup:
i) Enemies on the west coast of India like the Portuguese of Goa, the Siddi of Janjira and the British factors of Surat and Rajapur created obstacles in the work of expanding the Swaraj.
ii) It was necessary to control their activities and to protect the west coast.
iii) Maharaj had great foresight and realised that the one who has a navy, controls the sea. Hence, Shivaji Maharaj raised a navy.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj is regarded as an inspiration for freedom.
answermarkup: Because his struggle for Swaraj encouraged others, like Chhatrasal of Bundelkhand, to fight for independence. His efforts symbolized patriotism, courage, and self-rule, inspiring future generations and national leaders.

markup: After the death of Sambhaji Maharaj, the Marathas intensified their war with the Mughals.
answermarkup:
i. Aurangzeb was trying his best to defeat Sambhaji Maharaj. For this, he placed Mukarrabkhan in charge of the Kolhapur province.
ii. Mukarrabkhan learnt that Sambhaji Maharaj was at Sangameshwar in Konkan. He raided the place and captured Sambhaji Maharaj.
iii. When Sambhaji Maharaj was captured from Sangameshwar by Mukarrabkhan and taken to Aurangzeb, he faced Aurangzeb fearlessly.
iv. By the Emperor's orders, Sambhaji Maharaj was brutally put to death on 11^"th "  March 1689.
v. This Maratha Chhatrapati did not compromise his self respect and faced his death nobly and bravely.
This sacrifice of the Maratha Chhatrapati inspired the Marathas to intensify their fight against the Mughals.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj is called the founder of Swaraj.
answermarkup: Because he fought against powerful rulers like the Adilshahi, Siddis, Portuguese, and Mughals, and established an independent and sovereign kingdom that worked for the welfare of the people.

markup: In a democracy, citizens have a dual responsibility.
answermarkup:
i. Democracy gives the citizens various freedoms and rights.
ii. The citizens have to be vigilant about the unfair restrictions on their rights.
iii. At the same time, they are also expected to fulfil some duties and responsibilities.
Hence, we can say that in a democracy, citizens have a dual responsibility.

markup: Children below 14 years of age cannot be employed in factories or mines.
answermarkup: Because child labour leads to exploitation and harms children’s health and education. The Right against Exploitation protects children and ensures they get their Right to Education.

markup: The Right to Liberty is important for every individual.
answermarkup: Because it guarantees personal freedom such as speech, expression, and movement. It helps individuals to live freely, develop their abilities, and participate in democracy.

markup: Rana Pratap has become immortal in history.
answermarkup:
i) During Akbar's reign, Udaysingh - the father of Rana Pratap - was the king of Mewad.
ii) After Udaysingh's death, Maharana Pratap ascended the throne of Mewad and continued the struggle for Mewad's existence.
iii) He continued the struggle with Akbar to maintain his independence, till the very end.
iv) He displayed qualities of valour, courage, self-respect, sacrifice, etc.
These qualities have made him immortal in history.

markup: Women's life in Maratheshahi was difficult.
answermarkup:
i. In Maratheshahi, the women's life was full of hardships.
ii. Their world was limited to their parent's home and then their husband's home.
iii. Education of the women was completely neglected. Very few like, Veermata Jijabai, Maharani Yesubai, Maharani Tarabai, Umabai Dabhade, Gopikabai, Punyashlok Ahilyabai had achieved education.
iv. Moreover to that, certain customs like child marriage, unequal marriage, widowhood, keshwapan, sati, polygamy made their lives difficult.

markup: Before the times of Shivaji Maharaj, it was a great challenge to bring back the devastated life of the people to normalcy.
answermarkup:
i) Before the times of Shivaji Maharaj, the conflicts between various powers had created instability and insecurity in Maharashtra.
ii) Many a times the Watandar officers misused their powers which resulted in harassment of people.
iii) Agriculture was dependent on rainwater. If it did not rain, crops got destroyed due to lack of water. The shortage of foodgrains and fodder for cattle occurred.
iv) The famine that occurred in 1630 CE was a great calamity for the people. It led to hunger, scarcity of resources, poverty and many other hardships for the people. Entire families got destroyed, cattle & farm animals died and agriculture was devastated. It also put an end to the industries. All financial transactions came to a halt and people had to wander to faraway places in search of livelihood.
Due to all these reasons, it became a great challenge to bring back the devastated life of the people to normalcy.

markup: The Maratha rule came to an end.
answermarkup:
i. After the death of Mahadji Shinde and Nana Phadnavis, the Maratha power began to weaken.
ii. Bajirao II, the son of Raghunathrao was the Peshwa at that time. He did not have leadership qualities and had many vices.
iii. He was unsuccessful in uniting the Maratha Sardars and the internal conflict between the Maratha sardars weakened their power.
iv. The British replaced the Marathas in the North and South.
v. In 1817 CE, the British captured Pune and hoisted their flag 'Union Jack' there.
vi. In 1818 CE the British defeated Marathas in the battle of Ashti in Solapur district.
By this, the Maratha rule came to an end.

markup: The Marathas faced defeat in the Battle of Panipat.
answermarkup:
i. Vishwasrao was hit by an enemy bullet in the battle of Panipat.
ii. Sadashivraobhau went into frenzy on hearing this and fiercely attacked the enemy.
iii. But Sadashivraobhau disappeared in the battle fray and thereafter the Maratha soldiers lost their courage in absence of their leader.
iv. Taking advantage of this, the reserve contingents of Abdali launched an attack on the Marathas with a fresh vigour.
Thus, the Marathas faced a brutal defeat in the Battle of Panipat.

markup: After capturing Raigad from Maratha, the Mughal forces were at their wits' end.
answermarkup:
i. Raigad was captured in November 1689 and Maharani Yesubai and Shahu were arrested. Moreover, Aurangzeb had tempted many Maratha Sardars to join his side by offering them watans and jagirs. The situation became extremely critical for the Marathas.
ii. However, Rajaram Maharaj gave Mughals the taste of their own medicine by using their tactics against them and turned the tables around for Marathas. He promised that if a Maratha Sardar captured any Mughal territory it would be given to him as a jagir. This promise of jagir brought forward many capable Maratha Sardars.
iii. They invaded the Mughal territory with all their vigour, defeated many Mughal Generals and captured their territories.
iv. Santaji and Dhanaji were at the forefront in these actions. On one occasion, they even cut and carried away the golden pinnacle of the Emperor's own tent in a surprise attack. The huge artillery and war materials of the Mughals could not sustain against such surprise attacks and guerrilla tactics.
This concludes that post capturing Raigad from Maratha, the Mughal forces were at their wits' end.

markup: Why is the Bhakti Movement considered important in Indian society?
answermarkup:
1. The Bhakti Movement preached devotion to God instead of giving importance to rituals and caste distinctions.
2. It promoted equality, humanity, religious harmony, and unity among people of different religions and communities.
3. Saints spread their teachings in regional languages, making them easy for common people to understand.
4. It encouraged social reforms and contributed to the development of regional languages and literature.

markup: A pension scheme is implemented for old people.
answermarkup:
i. According to a provision in the Constitution, it is imperative on the State to offer public assistance to citizens in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, etc.
ii. It is mentioned as one of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
iii. A pension scheme ensures financial help to the enrolled citizens above 60 years of age.
Hence, a pension scheme is implemented for old people.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj entered into the Treaty of Purandar.
answermarkup:
i) To keep a check on increasing activities of Shivaji Maharaj, Aurangzeb sent Mirzaraja Jaisingh to Pune.
ii) Jaisingh sent Mughal forces to various parts of the Swaraj to capture the forts that Shivaji Maharaj possesed. These forces severely damaged the territories of the Swaraj.
iii) Shivaji Maharaj began preparations to crush his ravage. However, Jaisingh and Dilerkhan laid siege to the fort of Purandar.
iv) Murarbaji Deshpande tried hard to resist the Mughals at Purandar but he died a hero's death in this.
Considering the seriousness of the situation, Shivaji Maharaj entered into a Treaty of Purandar.

markup: Free and compulsory education has been made available to children in the age group 6 to 14.
answermarkup:
i. As per our Constitution, all children between 6 and 14 years of age are entitled to get education as a Fundamental Right.
ii. However, some of them have to work to help their parents earn a living for the family.
iii. In spite of these adverse conditions, as per the Right to Education Act, receiving education is extremely necessary for these children.
Hence, free and compulsory education has been made available to children in the age group 6 to 14 .

markup: Our history books and those of our parents and grandparents differ to a certain extent.
answermarkup:
i) History is written with the help of different sources of history viz. material, written and oral sources. 
ii) Even after it has been written down, the data is continuously researched.
iii) As and when this research throws light on any new information, history has to be revised accordingly.
As a result of these revisions, our history books and those of our parents and grandparents differ to a certain extent.

markup: The Hindawi Swaraj was founded by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
answermarkup:
i) Shivaji Maharaj wanted to establish a State that would ensure the welfare of common people.
ii) He aimed to remove oppression and injustice.
iii) He wanted to protect the Maharashtra Dharma and preserve the culture and freedom of the people.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj drew up a bold plan regarding Lal Mahal.
answermarkup:
i) Shaistakhan set up his camp at Lal Mahal in Pune where Shivaji Maharaj had lived in his childhood.
ii) Khan's forces looted the people in the regions around Pune.
iii) Two years passed, but Khan was not leaving Pune; which had an adverse effect on the people's morale.
iv) In these circumstances, Shivaji Maharaj drew up a bold plan and decided to raid Lal Mahal secretly.

markup: The Constitution prevents the imposition of religious taxes.
answermarkup:
i. Taxes that might be used to encourage a particular religion are called as religious taxes.
ii. India is a secular country and one of our fundamental rights is the right to freedom of religion.
iii. Accordingly, each Indian citizen has the freedom to practise any religion.
iv. In order to broaden the scope of the right to freedom of religion, the Constitution prevents the imposition of religious taxes.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj established the Council of Eight Ministers.
answermarkup:
i) After the foundation of Swaraj, Shivaji Maharaj crowned himself and expanded the boundaries of Swaraj up to the southern states through his campaign 'Dakshin Digvijay'.
ii) The Swaraj expanded and included large areas of Nashik, Pune, Satara, Sangli, Kolhapur, Sindhudurg, Ratnagiri, Raigad, Thane districts and also some parts of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
iii) An efficient administration was set up by Maharaj, to ensure the smooth management of the affairs of the Swaraj as well as the welfare of the people.
iv) The administration was divided into eight departments and a head was appointed for each department. These eight ministers formed the Council of Eight Ministers or the Ashtapradhan Mandal.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj decided to acquire the forts within his own jagir.
answermarkup:
i) In those days, forts were of special significance from point of view of establishing the power.
ii) It was believed, "If one had the forts, one ruled the land", because with a firm hold over a fort, it was possible to control the surrounding area.
iii) The forts situated within the jagir of Shivaji Maharaj were under the control of Adilshah. So capturing the forts was like challenging the Adilshahi.
iv) But for the foundation of Swaraj, such forts were needed.
Therefore, Shivaji Maharaj decided to acquire the forts that were within his own jagir.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj made the Surat Campaign.
answermarkup:
i) Surat was a big trade centre and port under Mughal control.
ii) The British, Dutch and French had their factories in Surat.
iii) It was a rich city and maximum revenue was being generated by this city for the Emperor.
iv) In three years' time, Shaistakhan had ravaged large territories of the Swaraj. To make up this loss and to teach the Mughals a lesson, Shivaji Maharaj made the Surat Campaign.

markup: Shahu Maharaj was able to win the support of many Maratha Sardars.
answermarkup:
1.	He was the grandson of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, so many Sardars respected his lineage.
2.	Balaji Vishwanath convinced Sardars that Shahu was the rightful heir.
3.	Shahu’s victory at the Battle of Khed strengthened his claim to the throne.
4.	His wise and diplomatic leadership united many Maratha nobles under him.

markup: The Constitution has entrusted the responsibility of conducting elections to an independent machinery.
answermarkup:
i) India is a democratic country. Accordingly, people have to elect their representatives periodically. This calls for conducting the elections.
ii) Conducting elections requires a free and fair atmosphere so that the citizens are able to elect a candidate of their choice without any fear or pressure.
iii) Such free, fair and just atmosphere for the elections cannot be guaranteed if the government itself conducts the elections.
Hence, the Constitution has entrusted the responsibility of conducting elections to an independent machinery, called the Election Commission.

markup: Ahilyabai Holkar is known as an ideal ruler.
answermarkup:
•	She looked after her people with care and justice.
•	She improved agriculture by digging wells and building lakes.
•	She encouraged trade and industry.
•	She built temples, ghats, and dharamshalas at pilgrimage places.
•	She ruled efficiently for 28 years and made her people happy.

markup: A conflict between the Marathas and Abdali was inevitable.
answermarkup:
i. The threat of Abdali was thwarted due to the Marathas and hence the Mughal Emperor gave them the chauthai rights to the Mughal Subhas including Kabul, Kandahar and Peshawar.
ii. These were previously Mughal Sabhas, however currently they were part of Abdali's Afganistan.
iii. As per the treaty of 1752 , it was the duty of the Marathas to win these Subhas back from Abdali and annexe them to the Mughal empire.
iv. On the other hand, Abdali wanted to bring the region upto Punjab under Afghan control.
Hence, a conflict between the Marathas and Abdali was inevitable.

markup: The Right to Equality ensures equal protection of the laws.
answermarkup: Because every citizen, regardless of caste, religion, sex, or place of birth, must be treated equally by the law. This right removes discrimination and promotes fairness in society.

markup: Fundamental rights are essential for democracy.
answermarkup: Because they protect the liberty, equality, and dignity of citizens, prevent misuse of power, and ensure that all citizens can live freely and equally under the law.

markup: The Nizam was defeated by Bajirao I at Palkhed.
answermarkup:
1.	Nizam tried to stop the Marathas from collecting Chauthai and Sardeshmukhi.
2.	He captured parts of Pune Pargana to challenge Maratha power.
3.	Bajirao used swift cavalry movements and avoided direct confrontation.
4.	His clever military tactics forced the Nizam to surrender and accept Maratha rights.

markup: Oral sources reveal various aspects of people's lives.
answermarkup:
i) The various forms of literature like owis, folk songs, folk tales, legends etc. which are traditionally passed on from one generation to the other by the word of mouth are called as oral sources of history. Such folk literature narrates about various aspects of the folk life of the people.
ii) They also help us understand various historical events, the policies and administrations of various rulers and the diplomatic relations between them.
iii) They throw light on the religious co-ordination, cultural aspects, etc. of that period. Thus we can say that, oral sources reveal various aspects of people's lives.

markup: A war between the Marathas and the British ensued.
answermarkup:
i. After Peshwa Madhavrao, Peshwa Narayanrao and Peshwa Sawai Madhavrao were in the grip of family feuds.
ii. Ragunathrao, who had once strengthened the Maratha power at Attock, sought shelter with the British to satisfy his greed for power.
iii. This led to a war between the Marathas and the British.

markup: The Constitution has abolished the practice of untouchability.
answermarkup: Because untouchability created inequality and discrimination in society. To establish equality and ensure that every citizen is treated with dignity, the Constitution abolished untouchability by law.

markup: The military strength of Sambhaji Maharaj was weakened.
answermarkup:
i. The wealth and army of the Adilshahi and Qutubshahi kingdoms conquered by the Mughals, made the already mighty Aurangzeb even stronger.
ii. He then concentrated all his might on defeating the Marathas and attacked their territory from all sides.
iii. The Maratha army General Hambirrao Mohite got killed during one of the encounters.
iv. The death of Hambirrao Mohite was a huge blow to the Maratha army and as a result, the military strength of Sambhaji Maharaj was weakened.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj is considered a great administrator.
answermarkup: Because he established a just, efficient, and welfare-oriented administration, cared for the ryot, enforced law and order, and created a system that ensured equality and prosperity for all.

markup: The villages during the Maratha period were self-sufficient.
answermarkup:
i) Most people in villages were engaged in agriculture and local occupations.
ii) They produced their own food grains and goods needed for daily life.
iii) Only a few items like salt had to be imported from outside.

markup: Shivaji Maharaj paid attention on building a Navy.
answermarkup:
i) After the victory of Javali, the activities by Shivaji Maharaj increased in Konkan.
ii) He captured Kalyan and Bhiwandi on the Konkan coast.
iii) There he came in contact with the Siddi, Portuguese and British powers on the Western Coast.
iv) He then realized that, in order to fight these powers, it was necessary to have a strong naval force.
Therefore, he concentrated on building a Navy.

markup: Maharaj's greatness is comprehensive.
answermarkup:
i. Shivaji Maharaj had many brave and loyal associates with him. Inspite of that, he independently faced many adversities and threats to Swaraj. Seeing his courage and valour, his associates were inspired to sacrifice their lives for Swaraj.
ii. His greatness transcended the quality of courage. He also aspired for an ethical and a qualitative base for the Swaraj.
iii. He paid attention to even minor issues along with the important ones, and gave orders regarding them. e.g.: The order that prohibited soldiers from taking vegetables from the fields of the peasants by force.
iv. He also imposed restrictions on the cutting of trees.
v. He severely punished those who would misbehave with women and took care of all sections of the society like farmers, craftsmen, soldiers, traders, merchants, etc.
vi. He was not just a great warrior, but also a great sculptor who created a new, independent, ethical and cultured society.
Hence, we can say that Maharaj's greatness is comprehensive.

markup: There was political instability and insecurity in Maharashtra at the beginning of the seventeenth century.
answermarkup:
i) The Nizamshah of Ahmadnagar and Adilshah of Bijapur ruled most of the territories in Maharashtra at the beginning of the seventeenth century CE.
ii) The Mughals had entered Khandesh and wanted to rule the south.
iii) The Siddi people from Africa had made settlements along the Konkan coastline.
iv) The Portugese had established their rule in Goa and Vasai on the western coastline.
v) The British, French and Dutch had set up factories through trading companies.
vi) All these powers had competition and conflict with each other.
All these factors had created political instability and insecurity in Maharashtra.

markup: A Constituent Assembly was established.
answermarkup:
i) The leaders of the freedom movement wanted Independent India to be governed by laws made by Indians themselves, and not by the British.
ii) It was decided that the Constitution of Independent India would be prepared and a Committee, known as the Constituent Assembly was established for this purpose.
iii) The process of the making of the Indian Constitution started in 1946.
iv) The representatives of the provinces and the princely states were included in this committee. There were a total of 299 members in the Constituent Assembly and Dr. Rajendra Prasad was its President.
In this way, a constituent assembly was established.

markup: The Marathas helped the Mughal power instead of fighting against it.
answermarkup:
1.	After Aurangzeb, Mughal rulers had stopped the policy of destroying the Marathas.
2.	The Mughals were weak and needed military help against internal and foreign enemies.
3.	Shahu Maharaj decided to protect the Mughal empire to expand Maratha influence peacefully.
4.	The Marathas believed that saving the old empire was as good as creating a new one.

markup: The Indian Constitution did not make the directives binding upon the State like the fundamental rights.
answermarkup:
i. The need to transform India into a developed and a progressive nation, called for drawing up and implementing new policies.
ii. These policies had to urgently address certain aspects of public welfare and hence, were prioritised through the Directive Principles of Sate Policy.
iii. Implementing all of these policies at the same time would have required a lot of resources. Hence, they had to be implemented slowly and steadily.
Due to the above reasons, the Indian Constitution did not make the Directives binding upon the State like the fundamental rights.

markup: Why does the Government function at two levels in a federation?
answermarkup:
i) The system, in which the administration of a country is cooperatively run by governments at two levels i.e. the Federal or Central level and the State level, is called as federalism or a federation.
ii) Looking after the administration of a territory as large as India, from a single capital city is difficult and may also lead to the neglect of some far-flung areas.
iii) Citizens of such far-flung areas are not able to participate in the affairs of the Government.
iv) To avoid this, the Government functions at two levels in a federation like India having a large territory and a huge population.

markup: Religious education cannot be made compulsory in government-aided schools.
answermarkup: Because the Constitution ensures freedom of religion and maintains secularism. Compulsory religious education would violate this principle by promoting a particular faith.

markup: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar is called the 'Architect of the Indian Constitution'.
answermarkup:
i) Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar was a pioneer in drafting the Indian Constitution.
ii) He was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee and had done a detailed study of the Constitutions of different countries of the world.
iii) He contemplated day and night to draft our Constitution.
iv) When the draft was ready, he presented the draft in the constituent Assembly, answered the various questions raised on it, made the required changes in the draft and made every provision flawless. Due to this enormous contribution towards the making of the Constitution, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar is called the 'Architect of the Indian Constitution.'
